# netcup_failover_ip_route (Resource)

Routing of a failover IP (v4 or v6) to a server (SCP REST API). Routing is asynchronous; the provider waits for completion.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Look up failover IPs, then route one to a server.
data "netcup_failover_ips" "all" {}

resource "netcup_failover_ip_route" "primary" {
  failover_ip_id = one([for ip in data.netcup_failover_ips.all.ipv4 : ip.id if ip.ip == "203.0.113.200"])
  server_id      = 12345
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `failover_ip_id` (Number) Id of the failover IP (from the `netcup_failover_ips` data source).
- `server_id` (Number) Server id to route the failover IP to.

### Optional

- `ipv6` (Boolean) Set to true for an IPv6 failover. Defaults to `false`.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Composite id `v4|v6/failover_ip_id`.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import format: v4/<failover_ip_id> or v6/<failover_ip_id>
terraform import netcup_failover_ip_route.primary v4/1234
```
